stem_text: A body is moving unidirectionally under the influence of a constant power source. Its displacement in time t is proportional to :

candidate_solve.initial_condition_status: PHYSICAL_CONDITION_TO_VERIFY (Initial rest v(0)=0 assumed for integration; not explicitly stated in stem).
candidate_solve.assumed_parameters_from_coaching_figure: None required (pure text). Body assumed to start from rest at t=0.
candidate_solve.derivation: Constant power P = F * v = m * v * (dv/dt) = constant. Separating variables: v dv = (P/m) dt. Integrating both sides: 1/2 v^2 = (P/m) t => v = sqrt(2P/m) * t^(1/2). Since v = ds/dt: ds = sqrt(2P/m) * t^(1/2) dt. Integrating from rest: s = sqrt(2P/m) * (2/3 t^(3/2)) => s proportional to t^(3/2).
candidate_solve.limiting_cases: If acceleration were constant (constant force), P = F*a*t proportional to t, and s proportional to t^2. Under constant power, acceleration decreases as v increases, yielding s proportional to t^(3/2), which is intermediate between t and t^2.

sl2.crux: Setting up the differential relation for constant power P = m v (dv/dt) and integrating twice to find displacement time scaling s proportional to t^(3/2).

concept_model_selection.evidence: Constant mechanical power model P = F v.

representation_translation.evidence: Converting rate of work statement into differential equation.

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Power rule integration: int t^(1/2) dt = 2/3 t^(3/2).

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Trap of confusing velocity scaling t^(1/2) with displacement, or assuming constant acceleration t^2.

wrong_route_hypotheses.route: Assuming constant acceleration s proportional to t^2 (Option D)
Taking velocity relation v proportional to t^(1/2) and inverting to t^(2/3) (Option A)
